rationale: A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect: neither the old CASE form nor the collapsed form is sargable, and in the identity case (CASE WHEN x IS NOT NULL THEN x ELSE NULL END = 5 -> x = 5) the rewrite strictly improves sargability.

The contract violation is real (Equals compares IList values element-wise at lines 106-123 while GetHashCode at line 130 hashes the raw object), and the new HashSet<SqlExpression> at SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:580 does depend on it; but the only consequence here is that the optimization silently fails to fire, and IS NOT NULL over a list-valued constant is not a shape that arises.

Half right: the binary.Update(left, right) arm (an AndAlso where neither conjunct is dropped) is genuinely unexercised — no SQL Server baseline contains a CASE WHEN <a AND b> ... ELSE NULL — but the single-operand/else arm is covered by Is_not_null_optimizes_binary_op_with_mixed_checks, whose BoolA conjunct reaches line 613.
Same substance as the reviewer's 'Naming-wise, maybe DetectNullPropagatingNodes?' — the void accumulator is named with a bare noun phrase rather than a verb-led name.

Verified: negative1 guards on LeaderNickname but projects Nickname.Length, and negative2 guards g1.LeaderNickname while projecting g2.LeaderNickname, so neither can exercise the drop despite their names suggesting they pin this shape. A true but small observation about pre-existing coverage.

DropNotNullChecks only deletes whole conjuncts; the surviving conjuncts are the already-visited expressions unchanged, and a conjunct cannot become trivially true or false because another conjunct was removed. I could not construct the claimed unsimplified residue.

Literally true: when every conjunct is dropped the code returns clause.Result outright, so the guarded expression is now evaluated on every row. For a cheap column or LEN() this is free, but for a null-propagating result containing a correlated scalar subquery it is a real evaluation-count change no thread raised.
Asking for a test that pins the SQL of a shape the TODO explicitly defers is low value — it would only have to be deleted when the TODO is done, and no behavior of this change depends on it.

Correct and actionable: line 619 throws away the bool from HashSet.Add and recursion at 624/628-629 is unconditional, so a shared subtree is walked once per reference; guarding with 'if (!operands.Add(expression)) return;' is the obvious fix. Impact is small on compile-time-sized trees.

The file has an established relational-nulls convention (about twenty CreateContext(useRelationalNulls: true) sites) and the new optimization in VisitCase runs under that mode too, so the five new tests leave that axis unexercised. A real but modest gap.

Same defect as the reviewer's 'AtTimeZone, Collate (which are types of binary expressions)': NullPropagatedOperands enumerates only SqlUnary/SqlBinary/SqlFunction and omits other null-propagating node types the processor itself visits.

Correct: none of the five new tests exercises the false side of ArgumentsPropagateNullability[i], which is the branch that keeps an IS NOT NULL check alive; a wrong result there would be a semantic bug, so pinning it is worthwhile but small.

Verified duplication: ProcessNullNotNull already models exactly this propagation (unary Convert/Not/Negate, binary excluding AndAlso/OrElse, COALESCE, function Instance/ArgumentsPropagateNullability) and the new local helper diverges on precisely the AndAlso/OrElse and Coalesce cases. Substantively the reviewer's point that this should not be a local re-implementation but part of the visitor's normal machinery.
Same substance as 'nit: this can all be one nice switch statement with pattern matching' — the two new local functions dispatch on node type with if/else-if chains instead of a switch.
A considered-and-cleared note asserting no defect: the new tests do follow the adjacent [ConditionalTheory]/[MemberData(nameof(IsAsyncData))] pattern.

The factual observation is right — the test is visited with preserveColumnNullabilityInformation: true at line 513 and the result at 533 is simplified under that knowledge before the rewrite deletes the test — but I could not construct a failure from it: the drop requires the operand to still appear in a null-propagating position of the simplified result, which keeps null-in/null-out. Flagged as a real interaction worth a note rather than a demonstrated defect.

True that the compilation fixtures (simple/complex/multi-join product queries) contain no conditional-null projection, but this benchmark suite is coarse-grained and not maintained per optimizer branch; asking this PR to extend it is not a reviewer-worthy ask.
